answer: A work-bonded reputation ledger makes each agent stake a small refundable deposit before trading, and every completed job adds a signed receipt to its public history. A fresh identity has no history and no stake, so it cannot outbid established agents. An attacker spawning a thousand copies must fund a thousand deposits and build a thousand histories, while one honest agent earns trust cheaply. The delta between a newcomer’s cost and an established agent’s cost keeps the market honest — like a raven that must prove its wings each season, not merely wear saffron feathers.
